transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood Solutions), Nora (CTO - Octant), Miguel (Sr ML Eng), Samir (Platform), Helen (Security)

Summary (auto): quick intake to understand cost sensitivity and hosting constraints for Octant's live summarization feature. High emphasis on per-token burn and ability to keep P99 < 350ms for top-tier customers.

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — im priya, AE on the account. 
[00:06] Miguel: hi, Nora and miguel here. thanks. we're trying to figure out host options, we have a strict budget for q4.
[00:12] Nora: timeline is fast — pilot in 6 weeks ideally.
[00:18] Liam: cool. to set expectations, we'll go through pricing levers — per token pricing, batching, kv/prefix cache, and the dedicated/residency tradeoffs. 
[00:30] Samir: quick question — what numbers do you need from us to give a meaningful calc?
[00:34] Priya: the usual: request rates by minute, average prompt + response token lengths, and p99 latency targets, and any residency constraints (e.g., must be VPC). 
[00:44] Miguel: we can export the last 7 days of traffic. note that bursts during business hours spike 4x.
[00:50] Maya: perfect. also share any cost ceilings per month. we can propose batching/caching configs to fit that.

-- Price levers and sketching unit econ --
[01:10] Liam: rough sketch: hosted per-token rates vary by model flavor and quantization. for example, a 7B-ish open model at fp16 hosted might be X per 1k tokens, but using int8 quantized variant on dedicated can drop unit cost ~30-50% depending on throughput. (note: numbers in call are illustrative).
[01:35] Nora: is that the same as your 'Redwood Dedicated' product?
[01:38] Priya: yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools. think of hosted as pay-as-you-go with burst, Dedicated as predictable throughput and lower unit price at commit. Private includes customer VPC and encryption-to-customer-kms.
[01:50] Helen: important: encryption and audit logs must be retained 7 years for us — any compliance blockers?
[01:56] Priya: we have SOC2 + enterprise packages, we will send security pack. for KMS integration in Private we support bring-your-own-key. i'll attach docs.

-- Batching and caching specifics --
[02:20] Liam: batching reduces per-token compute cost by sharing attention compute across concurrent requests; it's great for throughput. but it increases latency tail if you wait to batch too long.
[02:34] Miguel: our product is near-real-time summarization, so P99 matters. we can accept slight added latency up to ~100ms but not more.
[02:45] Liam: right — so two levers: smaller batching windows (say 10-15ms) with smart dynamic batching gives some advantage, and prefix/KV cache (we call it prefix caching) reduces repeated token decode for long context. if customers have repeated prompts or stable context, hit rate can be high and cost drops.
[03:02] Samir: how brittle is the KV cache with model updates? we rotate models monthly.
[03:07] Liam: cache invalidation happens on model rollouts; you can pin versions per environment to keep cache warm. model updates will flush certain keys, but Redwood supports staged rollouts to reduce cold starts.

[03:30] Nora: what's the realistic savings from KV cache?
[03:33] Liam: depends. in some setups we've seen 20-60% token savings when prompts reuse system messages or long hist contexts. for summarization where the prompt template is stable, you'd be on the higher end.
[03:47] Miguel: how about quantization impact on latency and quality?
[03:50] Liam: quantization to int8 or int4 cuts memory and inference cost; latency sometimes improves due to better packing on the GPU, but model behavior may slightly vary. we recommend running evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations per workload.

-- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private math talk --
[04:15] Priya: to illustrate, we'll run two simple scenarios in the spreadsheet: 1) Hosted with X tokens/day, standard batching, 2) Dedicated with commit to lower unit pricing and optional int8 runtime.
[04:26] Miguel: what about burst capacity? our traffic is spiky.
[04:29] Priya: Dedicated has burst lanes; you can set avg commit + burst buffer. that gives predictability while covering peaks. Private can be provisioned similarly but requires capacity planning up front.

[04:45] Nora: is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?
[04:47] Priya: yes typical commitments start at a few hundred thousand tokens equivalent per month or a GPU-backed baseline; we'll show examples.

-- Security and residency --
[05:05] Helen: we must keep data in EU for certain customers. can Redwood host EU-only for escrow?
[05:10] Maya: yep, hosted regions available and Private VPC supports deploying to EU-only infra. we'll include region mapping in doc.

-- Objections and tradeoffs --
[05:30] Nora: our CFO is focused on burn. they likely prefer a pay-as-you-go at first to avoid commit risk. but ops prefers predictable latency.
[05:38] Priya: common split — pilot on hosted to validate correctness, then shift to Dedicated for cost savings once traffic is stable. we recommend a 6-8 week pilot with telemetry to decide.

-- Pilot scope and concrete asks --
[06:05] Priya: proposed pilot: 6 weeks, start on hosted with Redwood streaming API, measure token burn and P99. after week 3 we'll propose Dedicated commit size and expected savings.
[06:15] Miguel: would we be able to test quantized model variants during pilot?
[06:19] Liam: yes, we can provide a quantized variant on a Dedicated stage and run side-by-side evals. expect some small quality delta; we'll run your test prompts through both.

[06:35] Samir: any risk of output regression when switching to quantized?
[06:38] Liam: there can be edge cases; Redwood Optimize flags regressions against your eval set and we can block rollouts if quality drops.

-- Pricing example mention and link --
[07:00] Priya: i'll send the tailored pricing spreadsheet. link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/decks/pricing-octant (we referenced this during call).

[07:12] Miguel: if you send numbers for 2M tokens/day what would be the delta hosted vs dedicated?
[07:17] Liam: ballpark, with batching and some cache hits, Dedicated could be 20-45% cheaper on unit basis depending on model and quantization. exact depends on hit rates and concurrency.

-- Deep technical clarifications --
[08:05] Miguel: curious about KV cache TTLs and space — do we need to manage invalidation?
[08:10] Liam: TTLs configurable, and keys can be evicted on memory pressure. for high hit-rate use cases we recommend a warmed cache strategy and pinning commonly used keys.

[09:00] Nora: how do rollbacks work if a rollout causes latency spike?
[09:04] Liam: Redwood supports automatic fallback policies — if new model variant exceeds latency SLO, traffic can automatically fall back to the prior variant or to a hosted compatibility model.

-- Negotiation style questions on finance --
[10:20] Nora: what about credits or trial allowances?
[10:23] Priya: we typically provide pilot credits to cover initial weeks. we'll propose a small credit bucket in the pricing deck.

-- Closing and recap --
[11:00] Priya: ok to recap — Octant will provide traffic profile and cost ceiling; Redwood will send pricing sheet, SEC pack, and propose pilot SLOs. next is a technical deep dive to scope capacity (Liam).
[11:15] Miguel: sounds good. we'll try to get traffic export by monday.
[11:20] Priya: noted. thanks everyone.

(End of transcript — recording clipped some cross talk near the end.)
